questions.stem: GANGA river originates from which glacier?
questions.explanation: GANGA river — TECHNICALLY the river is called 'BHAGIRATHI' from its source GANGOTRI GLACIER (snout: GAUMUKH, Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand) until DEVPRAYAG, where it MERGES with the ALAKNANDA river to BECOME the GANGA. ALAKNANDA itself rises from SATOPANTH + BHAGIRATH KHARAK glaciers near Mana, Chamoli district. THE 'PANCH PRAYAG' (5 sacred confluences along Alaknanda) — VISHNUPRAYAG, NANDPRAYAG, KARNAPRAYAG, RUDRAPRAYAG, DEVPRAYAG — last one creates Ganga. GANGA's COURSE: Devprayag → Rishikesh → Haridwar (where it enters plains) → Kanpur → Allahabad/Prayagraj (joined by Yamuna at SANGAM) → Varanasi → Patna → Bhagalpur → enters Bangladesh as PADMA → meets Brahmaputra (called JAMUNA in Bangladesh) → MEGHNA → Bay of Bengal. TOTAL LENGTH: ~2,525 km (longest river WHOLLY in India... actually it spans India + Bangladesh; INDUS is longer but mostly outside India; BRAHMAPUTRA is also long but starts in Tibet). LARGEST DRAINAGE BASIN in India: Ganga ~10 lakh sq km; covers UP, MP, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, WB, Delhi, Rajasthan, Haryana. UPSC angle: NAMAMI GANGE PROGRAMME (2014-) — pollution abatement; Ganga Action Plan. PYQ FREQUENCY: Ganga source in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: TRIVENI SANGAM at Allahabad/Prayagraj is the confluence of:
questions.explanation: TRIVENI SANGAM ('triple confluence') at PRAYAGRAJ (formerly Allahabad), Uttar Pradesh — confluence of: (1) GANGA — flowing from north (visible). (2) YAMUNA — flowing from west (visible). (3) SARASWATI — UNDERGROUND/MYTHICAL (not visible at surface; per legend, flows underground here). THIRD RIVER controversy: SARASWATI was a major Vedic river that DRIED UP ~4,000 BCE due to tectonic shifts (per geologists); identified with the Ghaggar-Hakra system. ATTRIBUTION VARIES: some say it's just spiritual presence; others say it actually emerges underground. KUMBH MELA: held at SANGAM every 12 YEARS (Maha Kumbh); ARDH KUMBH every 6 years; KUMBH ROTATES among 4 cities (PRAYAGRAJ, HARIDWAR, NASHIK, UJJAIN). PRAYAGRAJ 2025 KUMBH: ~40-60 crore pilgrims attended (largest peaceful gathering in human history). UNESCO recognized Kumbh Mela as INTANGIBLE CULTURAL HERITAGE OF HUMANITY (2017). HISTORICAL: AKBAR built FORT at Allahabad (1583) at confluence's strategic location — symbolic + strategic. FORT named ILAHABAD ('city of God'); renamed PRAYAGRAJ 2018 by UP government. UPSC angle: 'Saraswati' debates in NCERT history (Indus Valley civilization — was Harappan along Saraswati?). PYQ FREQUENCY: Triveni Sangam in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: BRAHMAPUTRA river is known by which name in TIBET (its source)?
questions.explanation: BRAHMAPUTRA — known by DIFFERENT NAMES through its course: (1) TIBET — YARLUNG TSANGPO (source: CHEMAYUNGDUNG glacier near Mt KAILASH, Tibet). Flows EASTWARD across S. Tibet for ~1,700 km (highest river in world by altitude). (2) Takes a U-TURN at NAMCHA BARWA peak (~7,800 m), forming the WORLD'S DEEPEST CANYON (Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon). (3) ARUNACHAL PRADESH (India) — called SIANG (as it enters India from north). (4) ASSAM — called BRAHMAPUTRA after merging with Dibang + Lohit at Sadiya. (5) BANGLADESH — called JAMUNA (different from Yamuna of north India!). (6) MERGES with PADMA (= Ganga in Bangladesh) at Goalondo → joint river called PADMA-JAMUNA. (7) MEGHNA — final stretch, into Bay of Bengal. TOTAL LENGTH: ~2,900 km (~700 km in India). LARGEST RIVER BY VOLUME in India (~1.5× Ganga's flow at Bay of Bengal). MAJOR FLOOD CHALLENGES — Assam annually devastated by Brahmaputra floods. KAZIRANGA NP gets ~80% inundated yearly. CHINA'S DAM CONCERNS: China is building MEGA DAMS on Tsangpo (e.g., 60-GW Medog dam, world's largest hydro project planned) — INDIA worries about water flow + flash-floods. NEPAL-BANGLADESH-INDIA water diplomacy concerns. UPSC angle: TRANSBOUNDARY RIVERS, water security; GS-2 IR with China, Bangladesh. PYQ FREQUENCY: Brahmaputra-Tsangpo link in UPSC, SSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: INDUS WATERS TREATY (1960) was signed between INDIA and PAKISTAN with mediation by:
questions.explanation: INDUS WATERS TREATY (IWT) — signed 19 SEPTEMBER 1960 in KARACHI by PM JAWAHARLAL NEHRU (India) and President AYUB KHAN (Pakistan). MEDIATOR: WORLD BANK (IBRD) — facilitated negotiations + provided technical assistance. KEY ALLOCATION: INDUS BASIN has 6 main rivers; treaty divides them: (1) EASTERN RIVERS (RAVI, BEAS, SUTLEJ) — fully to INDIA. (2) WESTERN RIVERS (INDUS, JHELUM, CHENAB) — substantially to PAKISTAN, with India having LIMITED USE rights (drinking, navigation, run-of-river hydropower without storage). KEY PROVISIONS: (a) PERMANENT INDUS COMMISSION — meets at least once a year. (b) DISPUTE RESOLUTION mechanism: bilateral commission → Neutral Expert → Court of Arbitration. (c) Treaty has SURVIVED FOUR WARS between India-Pakistan (1965, 1971, 1999 Kargil, near-war 2019, 2025) — testament to international water-treaty resilience. RECENT TENSIONS: (1) Pakistan complaints about KISHENGANGA (Jhelum tributary) and RATLE (Chenab) hydroelectric projects. (2) INDIA'S 2025 SUSPENSION/MODIFICATION threats post-Pahalgam terror attack — major diplomatic event. UPSC ANGLE: bilateral water treaties — treated extensively in GS-2 IR + GS-3 environment. OTHER WATER TREATIES: (a) GANGA TREATY 1996 with Bangladesh (Farakka water-sharing). (b) MAHAKALI TREATY 1996 with Nepal. (c) TEESTA — pending with Bangladesh. PYQ FREQUENCY: IWT in UPSC PT, Mains GS-2/3 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which is the LONGEST river of PENINSULAR INDIA?
questions.explanation: GODAVARI — LONGEST river of PENINSULAR INDIA; ~1,465 km. Called 'DAKSHIN GANGA' ('Ganga of the South'). SOURCE: TRYAMBAKESHWAR, Nashik district, MAHARASHTRA (in Western Ghats). FLOWS EASTWARD through MH, Telangana, AP into BAY OF BENGAL at delta near KAKINADA (AP). MAJOR TRIBUTARIES: Manjira, Pravara, Indravati, Wardha, Wainganga, Penganga, Sabari. DAMS: Polavaram (under construction, AP), Sriram Sagar, Pochampad, Jayakwadi. PENINSULAR RIVER LENGTHS (memorize): (1) GODAVARI — 1,465 km (longest). (2) KRISHNA — 1,400 km. (3) MAHANADI — 851 km (Odisha + CG). (4) KAVERI — 800 km. (5) NARMADA — 1,312 km (longest WEST-FLOWING peninsular; into Arabian Sea via Gulf of Khambhat). (6) TAPI — 724 km (also west-flowing). EAST-FLOWING vs WEST-FLOWING peninsular rivers: most east (Bay of Bengal); narrow Western Ghats divert SOME west (Narmada, Tapi, Mahi, Sabarmati, Periyar, Sharavathi). EAST-FLOWING form deltas (Krishna-Godavari is fertile rice-bowl); WEST-FLOWING form ESTUARIES (steep gradient, no deltas). UPSC angle: peninsular drainage system in NCERT class 9-10 + Indian Geography optional. CRITICAL: Krishna-Godavari basin is INDIA's RICE BOWL — MAJOR REGION for paddy, sugarcane. POLAVARAM PROJECT — multi-state project on Godavari, contentious. PYQ FREQUENCY: peninsular rivers in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: The NARMADA river flows through a unique geological feature called a:
questions.explanation: NARMADA flows through a RIFT VALLEY between the VINDHYA RANGE (north) and SATPURA RANGE (south). RIFT VALLEY: tectonic feature where land between two parallel faults has dropped down (graben). NARMADA is INDIA's only major river flowing in a rift valley. CONSEQUENCE: short tributaries (mountains close on both sides), no significant delta (steep gradient + estuary instead). LENGTH: ~1,312 km — INDIA's 5th longest river overall, LONGEST WEST-FLOWING peninsular river. SOURCE: AMARKANTAK plateau in MP (also source of Sone, which flows east). MOUTH: GULF OF KHAMBHAT (Arabian Sea), near Bharuch (Gujarat). KEY DAMS: SARDAR SAROVAR DAM (Gujarat, completed 2017 after decades of agitation); INDIRA SAGAR (MP); OMKARESHWAR + Mahesh­war + Bargi. NARMADA BACHAO ANDOLAN (NBA) — led by MEDHA PATKAR since 1989 — landmark social movement against Sardar Sarovar's height; argued for tribal rehabilitation, environmental concerns. SC ruled 2000 allowing dam to proceed (with monitoring). NARMADA's CULTURAL/RELIGIOUS importance: 'PARIKRAMA' (circumambulation) of Narmada is a sacred Hindu pilgrimage — ~3,500 km walk along both banks; takes 3-4 years. UPSC GEOGRAPHY: tectonic features in Indian peninsula — Aravalli (oldest); Vindhya + Satpura horst-graben system; Western/Eastern Ghats. PYQ FREQUENCY: Narmada rift valley in UPSC, SSC, NDA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The 'NATIONAL RIVER' of India, declared in 2008, is:
questions.explanation: GANGA — declared 'NATIONAL RIVER OF INDIA' in NOVEMBER 2008 by then-PM Manmohan Singh. KEY EVENTS regarding Ganga: (1) 1986 — GANGA ACTION PLAN (GAP) launched by Rajiv Gandhi govt. (2) 2008 — declared National River. (3) 2009 — NATIONAL GANGA RIVER BASIN AUTHORITY (NGRBA) established. (4) 2011 — World Bank loan for cleanup. (5) 2014 — NAMAMI GANGE Programme launched by Modi govt — ~₹20,000 crore initial; cleaning, ghats, sewage treatment, biodiversity, public participation. KEY POLLUTION SOURCES: (a) Untreated SEWAGE from cities (~2,500 MLD discharged into Ganga; only ~50% treated). (b) INDUSTRIAL effluents — tanneries (Kanpur), chemicals, textile. (c) AGRICULTURAL runoff — pesticides, fertilizers. (d) Religious offerings — flowers, plastics, ashes. RIVER GANGA BASIN: covers ~26% of India; populated by ~50 crore people; supports vast agriculture. NATIONAL AQUATIC ANIMAL: GANGES RIVER DOLPHIN (Platanista gangetica) — declared 2009; endangered; lives in Ganga + Brahmaputra. WORLD RIVERS DAY: 4th Sunday of September. INDIAN RIVERS UPSC angle: NAMAMI GANGE achievements + criticisms; biodiversity; tribal rights; transboundary water sharing. NATIONAL WATERWAYS — Ganga is NW-1 (Allahabad to Haldia, 1,620 km — used for cargo). PYQ FREQUENCY: Ganga as National River in UPSC, SSC, NDA, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The Bhagirathi River joins the Alaknanda River at which confluence to form the Ganga?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Devprayag is one of the Panch Prayag (five confluences) where Bhagirathi meets Alaknanda to form the Ganga.

questions.stem: The Chambal River is a major tributary of which river?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Chambal (originates in Madhya Pradesh) joins the Yamuna near Etawah in Uttar Pradesh.

questions.stem: The Ken River joins the Yamuna River after flowing through which state?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Ken River flows through MP and UP, joining the Yamuna near Banda; the Ken-Betwa river link project aims to connect these rivers.

questions.stem: The Son River is a right-bank tributary of which major river?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Son River (MP → Jharkhand → Bihar) joins the Ganga near Patna on its right bank; major tributary for the Bihar plains.

questions.stem: Which river, known as the 'Sorrow of Bihar', is notorious for frequent floods?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Kosi River ('Sorrow of Bihar') originates in Tibet/Nepal and shifts course frequently, causing devastating floods in north Bihar.

questions.stem: The Beas River was the eastern limit of Alexander the Great's campaign. Where does it originate?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Beas originates from Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass; it meets the Sutlej at Harike in Punjab.

questions.stem: The Betwa River finally joins which river near Hamirpur in Uttar Pradesh?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Betwa River (Vindhyas, MP) flows north and joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur, UP.

questions.stem: Tungabhadra is a major tributary of the Krishna River. It is formed by the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Tunga and Bhadra rivers (both originating in Western Ghats, Karnataka) join at Kudli/Shimoga to form Tungabhadra.

questions.stem: The Mahanadi Delta creates which distinctive geographical feature near the Bay of Bengal?

options.option_text: Chilika Lake (lagoon) and fertile deltaic plains

questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Mahanadi delta in Odisha forms fertile plains and isolates Chilika Lake (Asia's largest saltwater lagoon) from the sea.

questions.stem: The Damodar River, once called 'Sorrow of Bengal', originates in which state?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Damodar originates in the Chota Nagpur Plateau of Jharkhand and flows through Jharkhand and West Bengal into the Hooghly.

questions.stem: Periyar River is the longest river entirely within which state?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Periyar (244 km) is Kerala's longest river; the Periyar Tiger Reserve and Mullaperiyar Dam are on it.

questions.stem: Which river flows through the Shivpuri plateau and forms the Rajghat Dam before joining the Yamuna?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Betwa flows through Shivpuri (MP) with the Rajghat Dam; it joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur.

questions.stem: Ganga enters the Bay of Bengal through a large delta shared with Bangladesh. The distributary running through Bangladesh is called:
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: The Padma (Ganga's main channel in Bangladesh) joins the Jamuna (Brahmaputra) and Meghna before entering the Bay of Bengal.

questions.stem: The Subansiri River is a major tributary of the Brahmaputra and flows through which states?
questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Subansiri originates in Tibet, enters Arunachal Pradesh, and joins the Brahmaputra in Assam.

questions.stem: The Pamba River (Kerala) is associated with the famous Sabarimala pilgrimage. It ultimately drains into:

options.option_text: Vembanad Lake and then Laccadive Sea

questions.subject: Geography
questions.explanation: Pamba drains into Vembanad Lake (Kerala's largest lake) which is connected to the Laccadive Sea (Arabian Sea).
